name: MailScope AI — Security Snapshot
description: In-inbox forensic triage for Gmail, powered by the existing MailScope AI analysis backend. An interface layer only — all detection logic lives in the MailScope backend.

_permission_notes.storage: chrome.storage.local caches fingerprint -> analysis results locally, so re-opening an already-scanned email never re-calls the backend. No raw email content is stored, only the analysis result and a hash.
_permission_notes.activeTab: Grants temporary access to the active tab ONLY when the user opens the popup — used solely to check whether the active tab is Gmail and to relay a 'what's the current email's status' query to the content script. No background tab access, no browsing history.
_permission_notes.host_permissions: Limited to the MailScope backend origin(s) only, and only used by the background service worker to call the EXISTING /api/analyze and /api/reports endpoints. This also lets the background worker perform that fetch without being subject to Gmail's page-level CORS restrictions — no backend CORS changes were required. Add your deployed backend's origin here (and in shared/config.js) before shipping beyond localhost.
_permission_notes.explicitly_not_requested: cookies, history, webRequest, the broad 'tabs' permission, scripting, downloads, notifications, gmail.readonly OAuth scopes — none of these are used. The extension reads only what is already visible in the currently open Gmail message DOM.
